inspection_outcome: Verified failure of the explicit algorithm's core output guarantee; free-cokernel criterion not refuted
summary: Algorithm2 omits final node and death blocks, and its Proposition5 kernel-filtration subroutine shifts target indices. Exact legal inputs refute these central constructive guarantees. Algorithm1 and the main free-cokernel criterion remain counterevidence to whole-paper failure, not reasons to downgrade the demonstrated algorithm defect.
limitations: Full implementation and bit-complexity certification not performed.

source_claim.text: Algorithm2 returns an interval basis, while printed outer loop ends m-2 and inner loop ends m-1.

steps: Outer range1..0 empty, so beta1 stays empty.
True module is interval I_R^[1,2),requiring one basis vector.
For general m, line11 also uses Y_i^m absent from inner loop.

counterevidence: Algorithm1 p13 uses correct i<=m-1,j<=m ranges.
Lemma6 proof uses final death blocks.

impact.scope: Failure of the literal core algorithm guarantee; index repair available, free-cokernel criterion and Algorithm1 not refuted

correction.statement: Use outer1..m-1,inneri+1..m; align coherence/prose and known zero endpoint maps.

independent_verification.result: Confirmed: with m=2,f0=f2=0,f1=R all cokernels are free, but the outer loop is empty and beta1 remains empty. General line11 also needs the unconstructed Y_i^m. The abstract, Algorithm2 Ensure and Theorem9 explicitly promise an interval decomposition. Corrected ranges align with Algorithm1; no end-to-end code execution claimed.

assumptions: F_a=[0],F_(a+1)=[1],embedded at a1,m4 with zero endpoints and F3=0

steps: ker F_a=R,so stated block misses full initial kernel.

counterevidence: Corrected death-index construction follows successive unimodular SNF kernel/complement splits.

impact.dependency: Algorithm2 p15 line4 invokes Proposition5 to construct the kernel filtration; printed first block omits ker F_a and target index is shifted
impact.scope: Invalid subroutine supporting the core constructive algorithm; corrected death indexing restores the checked local induction without certifying an end-to-end implementation

correction.verification: Initial witness corrected and restricted-product induction verified analytically.
correction.limits: All terminal/proof indices must be reconciled; no executed implementation.

independent_verification.result: Confirmed: F_a represents target a+1, while the printed product with T_k^- ends at k+1 and omits T_a^-. F_a=0,F_(a+1)=1, embedded at a1,m4 with zero endpoints, has a full initial kernel but the printed first block has zero columns. Algorithm2 line4 uses Proposition5. Corrected death indexing and its local complement induction are valid; the main criterion is not refuted.

focused_acceptance_summary.scope: Focused independent challenge of Algorithm2 endpoint ranges and Proposition5 kernel blocks, including legal-input counterexamples, direct advertised algorithm/Theorem9 dependencies and the limits supplied by Algorithm1 and the free-cokernel criterion. Both report grades were corrected to Major. No complete algorithm implementation, full lattice proof or journal comparison was performed.
focused_acceptance_summary.assessment_review: Correct Minor to Major for both existing Problems and overall. The legal m2 instance directly refutes Algorithm2's central interval-basis output guarantee; its line4 invokes the defective Proposition5 filtration. Easy index repairs and survival of the independent criterion limit the damage but do not erase the core constructive failure.
